title: Tesla's Missing Autopilot Data Showed It Detected A Hazard Before Fatal Crash, Despite Claims It Was Missing

reading.body:
Tesla's Autopilot system was involved in a fatal crash. Tesla told the family that the vehicle's crash data had been deleted and was unavailable. A hacker later demonstrated that the data persists on Tesla vehicles and recovered it, showing the system had detected a hazard before the collision. This is a failure of data retention and retrieval in a safety-critical system, compounded by a false assertion to the family about what information could be recovered.

The recovered data became evidence in litigation. A jury found Tesla liable and awarded over $240 million in damages. A judge upheld the verdict. It is not established from these reports what specific failures in Autopilot behavior caused the crash itself, only that the system detected the hazard and that data about the event existed contrary to Tesla's claims.

This failure would have been caught by basic auditing of data storage practices before any statement was made to the family, or by maintaining accessible logs of what information persists on each vehicle. The system was deployed with insufficient verification of its actual data management capabilities relative to what was claimed.
